blocking_issues.location: PT-BR metadata tags/keywords and section 'Arquitetura legal e monetária'
blocking_issues.issue: The PT-BR edition exposes the raw English technical label 'currency board' repeatedly even though a natural Portuguese formulation is available. This violates the publication localization gate and makes the Portuguese edition read as partially untranslated.
blocking_issues.evidence: The staged PT-BR article says 'semelhante a um currency board' and the PT-BR tags/keywords also contain 'currency board'.

required_fixes: Localize 'currency board' in the PT-BR article and PT-BR metadata to a natural Portuguese expression such as 'conselho monetário' or, preferably for precision in this historical context, 'regime semelhante a um currency board (conselho monetário)' on first use followed by Portuguese wording thereafter. Preserve the IEO qualification that Argentina was not identical to the strictest classical currency-board design.

Do not change numbers, dates, causal framing, visual values or the factual conclusion while applying this editorial localization fix. If any material factual claim changes, resubmit it for full factual revalidation.
evidence: Argentina Law 23.928 confirms convertibility from 1 April 1991 at A 10,000 per U.S. dollar and the central bank conversion obligation.
Decree 2128/1991 confirms the peso denomination from 1 January 1992, 1 peso = A 10,000 and one peso per U.S. dollar for sale under Law 23.928.

IMF IEO confirms the regime's strong early disinflation, nearly 6% average real GDP growth during 1991-98, large capital inflows and the later interaction of fiscal weakness, foreign-currency debt, the peg and external shocks.
IMF IEO statistical material confirms CPI Dec/Dec values 84.0% (1991), 17.6% (1992), 7.4% (1993), 3.9% (1994), 1.6% (1995) and 0.1% (1996).
Visual budget passes: three Markdown tables, one explicit CPI bar chart and one causal flow are present in both locales, with equivalent values and structure.
notes: Factual and methodological spot checks passed for the central quantitative and legal claims reviewed. Rejection is publication-blocking but narrowly editorial/localization-related; no approval was created and no public surface was modified.
